source.commit_check: the trigger folders have the Git tree ids and the manifest digest recorded for this commit, the five quoted files have their recorded Git blob ids (CRLF normalised to LF), and the history has the recorded numbers of commits

encoding.files.event_files: per folder, one string per event file in file-name order: '<file name without .trigger.json> <details.run_id, or - when the file has none>'
encoding.history.events: one string per event file name that ever existed under state/triggers/ on the first-parent chain, in order of first appearance: '<file name without .trigger.json> <record> ...'. A record is +<folder>@<n> (added to the folder by commit n) or -<folder>@<n> (deleted from it); within one commit the deletions are listed first. Git was told not to pair a deletion with an addition (--no-renames), so a move is one of each in the same commit.
encoding.history.other_files: the same for the three files that are not events
encoding.history.n: position of a commit among the commits_read, oldest first, from 1
encoding.history.producer_commits: for each type named by a subject that matches producer_subject_pattern, the n of those commits; every other commit is listed in full under other_commits
encoding.folder: top = state/triggers itself, processing and archived = its two sub-folders
encoding.governed_paths: the paths of the driver's skill file and of the compounding-metrics policy are written with a space on each side of every slash, so that this data file is not counted as a citation of those two governed artifacts by scripts/evolution_metrics.py

files.source: the working tree, verified against the pinned commit by the three Git tree ids below
files.git_tree_id_rule: sha1 of the Git tree object rebuilt from the entries of the folder: every file as mode 100644 with blob id sha1(b'blob <size>\0' + bytes), CRLF normalised to LF, and the two sub-folders of state/triggers as mode 40000 with their own tree ids

history.source: git log at the pinned commit: commits and trees only, no file content of an old commit
history.first_parent_chain: the commits reached from the pin by following each commit's first parent: the successive states of the main branch. A merge appears once, compared with its first parent.
